doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: How he writes songs and what Nashville taught him
summary: He starts from a melody and writes lyrics last; Nashville taught him storytelling in lyrics.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. That was a shock. Well talk about your songwriting a bit. How do you start?

Sometimes I’ll get a title maybe or I’ll hear a phrase or something will pop into my head. More often than not I’ll hear some kind of little piece of melody or melody and a couple of changes, and then I’ll try and develop that. And normally the lyric kind of comes last, oddly enough — or maybe not oddly enough — but that’s kind of how I do it. And maybe the greatest thing that came out of my years in Nashville, I lived 4-1/2 years there, and a lot of the songs, they’re not maybe harmonically sophisticated. But the storytelling and the lyric is pure genius. And that I always felt was the weakest aspect of my writing. So by going to Nashville I became really aware of telling a story, not wasting the listener’s time, and trying to tell it, trying to create musical poetry. And it’s still my greatest challenge in songwriting.
Yeah because sometimes you read something and you almost — I could have done that. Well you should have.
It’s easier — this is one of the amazing things about art to me, is sometimes you hear something and you go yeah, what else could it be. But the genius that it takes to create
that what else could it be is mind-boggling and inspiring. You know, how do I tap into that.
